Article Title: 'Largely irrelevant': Jaishankar says UN failing on Gulf, Ukraine, Africa and Covid
Article Text:
File photo: EAM Jaishankar

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has called the United Nations “largely irrelevant” to decision-making on major global crises, blaming a “gridlocked” Security Council and its outdated composition for the organisation’s ineffectiveness.Speaking at the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on Monday, Jaishankar said the UN had struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues, including conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine, crises in Africa and the Covid-19 pandemic.“Where the UN is concerned, I think it's obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked,” Jaishankar said.“If you look at the big issues of the day... actually, the United Nations has been largely irrelevant to the decision-making,” he added.Jaishankar said much of the problem stemmed from the Security Council’s inability to reach decisions. He also questioned whether its current composition reflected the wider international community.The UN was founded with 51 members and now has almost four times that number, he noted.“So, if you have grown four times, and you want to keep the old board of management, it's not going to work. I mean, it's common sense,” he said.Jaishankar also criticised countries that he said were resisting UN reform while citing Africa’s interests as a reason.He said Africa had already presented a clear position during intergovernmental negotiations on what it wanted from reform of the world body.Despite his criticism, Jaishankar said the answer was not to bypass the UN.“We need the UN. The UN has done a big service to the international community,” he said.“Our job must be to ‘fix the UN, not to work around the UN’,” he added, saying the UN itself needed to contribute to the reform process.India has been pushing for comprehensive UN reforms, including expansion of the Security Council. It has worked with the G4 grouping of India, Japan, Brazil and Germany, as well as the L.69 group of developing countries, to build support for reform.Jaishankar has previously criticised the UN’s structure, saying the organisation had failed to keep pace with a world that had become more interconnected and multipolar.
Article Summary: External affairs minister s jaishankar says the un has struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues. He blames a “gridlocked” security council and its outdated composition for the organisation’s ineffectiveness. India has been pushing for comprehensive un reforms.

Article Title: Abhijeet Dipke claims CJP activists receiving police notices threatening October 10 protest 'could turn violent'
Article Text:
‘One nation, one political party’: Abhijeet Dipke targets Centre, alleges pressure on CJP activists

NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday targeted the centre and alleged that “One Nation, One Election” was merely a slogan and alleged that the government’s intention was to establish “one nation, one political party”.He also claimed that activists of the Cockroach Janta Party were being served police notices and pressured against participating in protests."I have said multiple times that the Maharashtra Police is the best police force in the country, and the Delhi Police should learn from them. But it is heartbreaking that the Chandrapur police served notices to CJP workers, telling them not to participate in the agitation at Jantar Mantar. They also asked about the source of the expenses for travelling to Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.Dipke questioned how police could predict that the agitation would turn violent. He also questioned the police directive to CJP activists against making social media posts that could allegedly lead to violence."We speak about (Mahatma) Gandhi and B R Ambedkar. Do they think it is violent?" he asked.The CJP had earlier welcomed the INDIA bloc’s proposed protest on Tuesday, saying its own October 10 mobilisation should be seen as a broader call by the youth rather than an event led by any particular organisation.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said everyone, including political parties, student organisations, activists and members of the public, should assert their rights through peaceful protests.CJP co-convener Saurav Das said the organisation welcomed the INDIA bloc’s planned protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Tuesday.“We welcome all peaceful protests. Everyone should make efforts, be it INDIA bloc or other student organisations or activists, or common people. Everyone needs to assert their rights,” Das told a press conference.Das said repeated protests indicated that people were not being heard. “If people are hitting the streets repeatedly then there is a problem,” he said, adding that taking to the streets was the “last resort” for people who felt their concerns were not being addressed.At the press conference, Das also claimed that the CJP had received information from “well-wishers” within the establishment that its leaders could be arrested ahead of the October 10 protest. “Well wishers have informed us that meetings are taking place and there is a high possibility that CJP leaders could be arrested,” he claimed. “It does not matter if we are arrested or detained because this fight is about the young generation.“Even if we are arrested or detained the protest will go on because this is the fight for our future,” he asserted. “Fear of FIR, fear of jail has evaporated -- it won't work anymore.”Das said Jantar Mantar had become a “symbol of hope and victory” and asserted that protesters would sit wherever police stopped them. “Wherever police stops us, we will sit there and that will become Jantar Mantar,” he said.Das also referred to the Supreme Court’s Monday remarks on the controversy surrounding Form 6, accusing the Election Commission of misrepresenting the court’s position. “The EC sought to clarify in its press statement that the Supreme Court upheld changes in Form 6. Today, the Supreme Court has said the EC lied,” he said.Chief Justice Surya Kant, during a hearing on Monday, said the Supreme Court had not approved any modification to Form 6. The clarification assumes significance as the EC, in its September 26 statement following a meeting of the full commission, had said the “declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court”.On the CJP’s October 10 mobilisation, Das said the protest should be viewed as a broader youth movement rather than the initiative of a particular organisation. “You should not consider the call for protests on October 10 as our call or someone else's call. This is the call by the youth and Gen Z. We are one part of that.”His remarks came against the backdrop of an online exchange over the weekend between the CJP and sections aligned with the Congress, after a social media post compared CJP national convener Abhijeet Dipke with AISA president Neha Bora. Dipke and Bora rejected any suggestion of rivalry, while CJP leaders accused sections of the “liberal ecosystem” of attempting to undermine Dipke.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj also weighed in, cautioning against replacing one form of “hero worship” with another.The exchange brought differences between the CJP and sections of the Congress into the open. Some Congress leaders have been wary of the CJP’s emergence, given the AAP background of several of its prominent faces, while the AAP has backed its recent mobilisations.
Article Summary: Cjp founder abhijeet dipke alleges that ‘one nation, one election’ was merely a slogan. He also claimed that activists of the cockroach janta party were being served police notices and pressured against participating in protests.

Article Title: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, time to resign': Rahul Gandhi as INDIA bloc march to EC stopped

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign as INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India headquarters over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,” Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X as he led the opposition MPs towards the ECI office.The march, which began from Parliament's Makar Dwar around 11 am, was stopped by security personnel near the Niti Aayog office. Several INDIA bloc MPs subsequently sat in protest, with opposition leaders later staging a dharna at Parliament Street.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule were among the opposition leaders participating in the march.Visuals showed Rahul Gandhi leading the march along with several INDIA bloc MPs, who were carrying placards and cutouts of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The opposition MPs were seeking Kumar's removal over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. The INDIA bloc had announced the march from Parliament to Nirvachan Sadan as part of its campaign against the Election Commission's handling of the electoral roll revision.The march was met with heavy security deployment in central Delhi. Barricades were placed along the route and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the protest.After being prevented from proceeding towards the ECI headquarters, several opposition MPs sat in protest near Parliament Street.AAP said it would skip the march, with the party saying it would fight the issue through its own means.Opposition steps up attack over SIRThe protest comes amid an ongoing political confrontation between the opposition and the Election Commission over the SIR exercise and alleged discrepancies in voter rolls.The Supreme Court on Tuesday said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 used for voter enrolment during the SIR process. CJI Surya Kant said, “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us.”The court issued notices to the Centre, ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and other officials while declining to pass an ex-parte interim order suspending Kumar.Ahead of the march, several opposition leaders criticised the Election Commission's handling of the SIR process. Congress and INDIA bloc leaders have demanded Kumar's removal, while the BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations.Mamata Banerjee has said the protests will continue until Kumar resigns and has also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation.Congress MP Jairam Ramesh had said the march would be peaceful. The opposition has also announced district-level padyatras till October 8 and "Save votes, save the country" rallies from October 25 to November 25.
Article Summary: 'gyanesh, it’s done, bro, time to resign,' rahul gandhi said in a post on x as he led the opposition mps towards the eci office. Several india bloc mps subsequently sat in protest, with opposition leaders later staging a dharna at parliament street.

Article Title: ‘Unacceptable’: India reacts after Russian strike injures Indian sailor on Black Sea ship
Article Text:
India has strongly condemned the attack on the MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea, which tragically resulted in the deaths of two foreign nationals

India on Monday condemned the attack on a civilian commercial vessel in the Black Sea as “completely unacceptable” after a Russian drone strike reportedly killed two foreign nationals and injured crew members, including an Indian sailor.The vessel, MV ROYAD MAMMADOV, was attacked outside Romania's territorial waters, according to reports. Three Indian nationals were among the crew, with the Indian Embassy in Romania confirming that all three were safe and receiving medical care.One of the three Indians was injured in the attack and was being treated at Constanța County Hospital. Indian Ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke with the three crew members and the hospital's chief physician, who confirmed that they were in good health and receiving necessary care.“All three Indian nationals are safe. We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,” the embassy said.External affairs minister S Jaishankar, speaking at the United Nations General Assembly, condemned attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers across major maritime routes.“New challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations. This is completely unacceptable,” Jaishankar said.The Indian mission said it was in contact with relevant authorities to establish further details of the attack and ensure the welfare of the Indian crew members.

NEW DELHI: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra on Tuesday accused Rahul Gandhi of misleading the public over Form 6. He alleged that the Congress and INDIA bloc were attempting to undermine constitutional institutions amid their planned protest against the Election Commission .Patra said the Supreme Court had not declared Form 6 illegal and had only agreed to examine allegations concerning changes to the form. He also rejected Gandhi's claim of differences within the Election Commission over the issue, citing an ECI fact-check that said the Bihar SIR order was approved unanimously."Rahul Gandhi posted today regarding Form 6 after the hearing in the Supreme Court on the PIL. This is an attack on the Election Commission, but the second line mentions the BJP as well, so the BJP will respond to it. We had not consented to any such changes. If any change has indeed been made, it will only become clear after the notice is issued," he said."Even after that, when we read the detailed order and look at the Election Commission's press release... it becomes clear that the Commission had explicitly stated that there was no change in Form 6, and the Supreme Court had upheld the associated declaration. Therefore, there is no ambiguity here. When Rahul Gandhi claims that Form 6 was illegal and that the Supreme Court said so today, he is lying," Patra added.Patra also hit out at the Congress and INDIA bloc over their planned march to the Election Commission, alleging that the opposition was seeking to weaken democratic institutions to facilitate Gandhi's political rise."A sponsored attempt is being made by opposition parties, especially the Congress, as to how a change of power can be brought about in the country and Rahul Gandhi be made to sit in power just like that. For this, a blow to India's democracy and constitutional bodies is being hurled in a sponsored manner," he said."After failing multiple times, Congress leaders decided to establish anarchy in the country and attack institutions... Today again, they are trying to create anarchy and undermine democratic institutions by allegedly marching towards the Election Commission," Patra said.He alleged that the Congress had been attempting for years to "launch and relaunch Rahul Gandhi", and accused the opposition of attacking institutions after failing to do so through electoral politics.On the alleged dissent within the poll panel, Patra said the Election Commission had clarified that its order on the Special Intensive Revision in Bihar was issued with the unanimous approval of all commissioners."The fact-check states that the order regarding SIR in Bihar was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. Subsequently, the Supreme Court of India upheld this order in its decision. It was indeed a unanimous decision with no room for doubt," he said.

Article Title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
Article Text:
What Bhuyan had said

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court."Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court."He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework."Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said."I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.Justice Bhuyan, who served as the Chancellor of NALSAR, on Sunday said he can be legitimately proud of the students of the institution."You have shown to the country and the world what a university student, that too, a student of law, should be like. You are brilliant. You are bold and you are brave," he said.
Article Summary: Former chief justice of india br gavai and other retired judges on monday condemned supreme court judge justice ujjal bhuyan's remarks on the election commission. Justice dhingra said bhuian's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" justice sodhi said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework.

He further demanded accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as well as other two election commissioners along with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah."More skeletons are tumbling out of the Election Omission of India’s closet. Article Title: US nuke test detection experiment bid to assert its hegemony: Ex-nuclear chief
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Former chief of Atomic Energy Commission of India, Anil Kakodkar, who played a key role in the Pokhran nuclear weapons tests, said the main aim of the US conducting what is called a non-proliferation experiment last week was to assert its global nuclear hegemony and prevent other nations from conducting atomic tests.On Sept 30, the US conducted an experiment which will enable it to detect whether countries are carrying out low-yield nuclear explosions.Kakodkar told TOI, “The US is attempting to get more sensitivity in terms of nuclear tests detection. There is a generic understanding that nuclear tests will not be carried out. But what if a country executes a test camouflaged?”Asked whether the motive of the test jeopardised nuclear sovereignty of countries, he said the main aim was to assert global US nuclear leadership and stop other countries from carrying out atomic weapons tests.A recent study by Federation of American Scientists says that currently India has 190 nuclear warheads and has enough military plutonium for 140 to 225 nuclear warheads.Anil Anand, considered the father of India’s nuclear submarine programme, quoted US National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) and told TOI that in the experiment researchers gathered measurements using a broad suite of advanced sensors, including accelerometers, seismometers, chemical and radiotracer samplers.He said, “Together these measurements will improve scientists’ understanding of the signatures produced by underground explosions and strengthen US’ ability to detect and characterise nuclear explosive events. ”According to NNSA, it “conducted a subsurface, non-nuclear chemical high-explosive experiment” at the Nevada National Security Site. An FB post by NNSA states, “If foreign countries test in secret, we will know.The goal? Keeping the US one step ahead.” It further said the experiment assumes significance in the context of China supposedly having conducted a nuclear test in June 2020 secretly.“It takes nuclear expertise to detect nuclear activities, and experiments like these ensure America remains unmatched in detection,” said Brandon Williams, NNSA administrator. “Trump Administration has made it clear that the US will lead from a position of strength. You cannot evade American innovation. With this experiment, we are sending a clear message that under this administration, America will never be outmatched. ”
Article Summary: Former chief of atomic energy commission of india, anil kakodkar, said the main aim of the us conducting what is called a non-proliferation experiment last week was to assert its global nuclear hegemony. On sept 30, the us conducted an experiment which will enable it to detect whether countries are carrying out low-yield nuclear explosions.

Article Title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief
Article Text:
The idea of an informal meeting with SC judges on simultaneous polls was first mooted by DMK MP and senior advocate P Wilson

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court had initially fixed a schedule for an "informal interaction" with members of the Parliament committee examining the bill for simultaneous elections, the panel's chairperson, P P Chaudhary, told reporters Monday, stating that the SC later found it "not appropriate" and called it off, apparently after some opposition MPs criticised the proposed meeting.He, however, defended the proposal, saying there were precedents of parliamentary committees interacting with SC judges because of their expertise and knowledge of constitutional matters.Sources said the idea to meet SC judges was first mooted by DMK MP P Wilson, a senior advocate, and was informally deliberated within the committee before it took this up with the SC.The meeting was fixed for October 6 but the SC secretary general last week informed the committee of the cancellation."They (senior SC judges) are of the opinion that as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review before the Supreme Court, it may not be expedient or desirable to discuss the issue on the administrative side. The proposed meeting is accordingly cancelled," the secretary general said.Chaudhary said an email was sent to the Parliament secretariat by SC officials on September 22, stating that a meeting had been fixed on October 6 at 4.30 pm and the law ministry also sent the relevant material to the court."After about eight or nine days, some issues were raised publicly. Later, SC cancelled the meeting. If SC felt it was not appropriate, there was no need to pursue the matter. There was no need to create or give further publicity to the issue. "Sources said, on September 18, the Lok Sabha secretariat first wrote to the SC secretary general, conveying the committee's desire to undertake a "local study visit" for "informal discussions" with the CJI and other judges on simultaneous elections.Wilson, through a seven-page letter to the committee, defended the proposal and said in the spirit of broad-based consultation, he had suggested that the panel hear the views of the CJI and other judges. "Unfortunately, due to political objections surrounding this meeting, it was decided to call off the meeting because of unnecessary and unfortunate circumstances caused by vested interests," he said. Opposition MPs, including senior advocate Kapil Sibal, had slammed the proposed meeting.
Article Summary: The idea of an informal meeting with sc judges on simultaneous polls was first mooted by dmk mp and senior advocate p wilson. The meeting was fixed for october 6 but the sc secretary general last week informed the committee of the cancellation. Opposition mps, including senior advocate kapil sibal, had slammed the proposed meeting.

Article Title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on sitting SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR

NEW DELHI: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's criticism of deletion of a large number of voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) process, when the issue is pending adjudication before Supreme Court , drew a sharp reaction from former CJI BR Gavai, who termed it judicial impropriety.The former CJI refrained from directly commenting on his former colleague's remarks, but stressed a sitting or retired judge of Supreme Court, high court or any court must not speak on matters that are pending adjudication before a court."I am of the firm view that judicial discipline and propriety do not allow any sitting or retired judge to speak something which pertains to issues pending adjudication before SC, HC or any court," Justice Gavai said when asked by the media about Justice Bhuyan's statement at Nalsar, Hyderabad Sunday on the SIR of electoral rolls.Besides Justice Bhuyan, former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman also criticised the intensive revision of rolls, saying a citizen's right to vote, which is at the heart of democracy, was at "great peril" because of "illegal knocking out" of people from voters' lists.The SIR exercise in West Bengal was challenged before SC, which upheld it after tweaking the process by first engaging judicial officers in the scrutiny of documents and then providing for a special appeal provision by constituting tribunals.However, petitions which challenge SIR in different states, where large-scale deletion of voters from draft rolls has taken place mainly because of "logical discrepancy" and "voter mapping" issues, are still pending in courts.Justice Bhuyan, speaking at Nalsar, had said that any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens is intrinsically arbitrary as it strikes at the heart of the Constitution.Former CJI Gavai said he does not want to comment on Justice Bhuyan's statement.Justice Bhuyan had said, "Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens making them citizens without voting rights would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of the Constitution.""If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary... No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution."

Article Title: India & Switzerland deepen ties across trade, mobility, tech and defence; sign 5 pacts

NEW DELHI: India and Switzerland looked to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, technology, defence production and nuclear energy as PM Narendra Nodi held talks with visiting Swiss president Guy Parmelin. The 2 countries also signed 5 agreements, including 1 for a migration and mobility partnership and another for exchange of young professionals.Identifying innovation, infrastructure, and advanced technology as strong pillars of the bilateral partnership, Modi said India and Switzerland were going to give the relationship a new momentum and take it to new heights.The 2 countries set up a committee to facilitate trade and investment and address trade-related concerns, building upon the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) signed between India and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries in 2024. TEPA was India’s first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe, as Modi recalled.“It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to achieve the targets of $100 billion in investment in India and 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years,” said Modi in his media statement.Key Highlights of TEPA included enhanced market access for Indian goods and services, $ 100 billion investment commitment over 15 years, creation of 1 million jobs in India and stronger bilateral relations with EFTA nations - Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.The leaders discussed the conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, with the Swiss president welcoming Modi’s message to Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war.Modi said India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue, and diplomacy and will continue to work together for global peace and stability.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace,” he said, adding that the leaders also agreed that reforms in global institutions are essential to address the growing global challenges.The PM said that the mobility agreement will open up many new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals, and young people. The mobility agreement provides for multiple-entry visas for upto 5 years, including stays of upto 6 months on each visit, and renewable 1-year student permits.Apart from the mobility agreement, the 2 sides also signed another MoU to govern the exchange of young professionals taking up temporary employment in the other country to enhance their professional and language skills within their field. According to the Indian government, the MoU incorporates exchange of 300 persons annually per country, which may increase to 500, and a timeline of 30/90 days for verification of nationality/residency status, among other provisions.Modi said both countries had taken several important decisions to increase market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries.“This will help increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract new Swiss investments into key sectors in India, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability,” said Modi, adding that through these initiatives, both countries will work together to develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the world.In his remarks, Parmelin said the partnership is mutually beneficial. “India gains from capital, technology transfers, and facilitated access to markets for high-value-added goods. Switzerland, for its part, benefits from exchanges with an immense partner experiencing sustained growth, at a time when global trade has become more exposed and unpredictable,” said Parmelin, who currently holds the rotating Swiss Confederation presidency.The PM thanked Parmelin for visiting India with a large business delegation and attending the “Prosperity Summit” that India will host this week with India-EFTA business leaders.“This summit will serve as an important platform to turn the promise of our trade and investment partnership into concrete outcomes. I also extend my very best wishes to all the business leaders participating in this summit,” he said.
Article Summary: Swiss president guy parmelin welcomed pm modi’s message to russian president vladimir putin to end the ukraine war. The 2 countries also signed 5 agreements, including 1 for a migration and mobility partnership and another for exchange of young professionals.

NEW DELHI: At least two people were killed and several crew members, including an Indian national, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire aboard a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea.The Indian Embassy in Romania said three Indian nationals were among the crew of the vessel, identified as MV Royad Mammadov, and that one of them was injured and receiving medical attention.“We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties (foreign nationals) while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members,” the embassy said in a post on X.The embassy said it was in close contact with the relevant authorities to establish further details about the safety and welfare of the Indian nationals.Indian ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke to the three Indian crew members who were receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. The embassy said the hospital's chief physician confirmed that all three were in good health and receiving necessary care.“Amb @manojifs spoke with the three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. He also spoke with the hospital’s Chief Physician, who confirmed that all three are in good health and receiving necessary care. The ambassador assured them of all possible assistance and support,” the mission said.It later said that all three Indian nationals were safe.“We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,” the embassy added.The nationalities of the two people killed in the incident were not immediately known.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that two Russian drones had struck a civilian vessel carrying corn in neutral waters.“A horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkiye,” Zelenskyy said.He said Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were aboard the vessel and that the ship's captain had been killed. The fate of another person was still being established, he said.“Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board. As of now, unfortunately, we know that the ship’s captain was killed. My condolences. The fate of one other person is still being established,” Zelenskyy said.He added that 11 crew members had been rescued, including one who was injured.Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly proposed concrete measures to de-escalate the conflict and improve security in the Black Sea.“Pressure is needed to restore global food security. And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help,” he posted.Romania's interior ministry said its Coast Guard was alerted about the fire at around 11 am local time after the vessel was reported in the country's exclusive economic zone, about 30 nautical miles (55 km) south of Sfantul Gheorghe in Tulcea County.The ministry did not confirm what caused the fire. Romanian media reported that the vessel had been hit by a drone southeast of a Black Sea oil platform, but the reports had not been immediately verified by authorities.Romania's Naval Authority identified the vessel as the Royad Mammadov. According to MarineTraffic, it is a general cargo ship flagged to Saint Kitts and Nevis. It had departed Ukraine's port of Izmail and was headed for Italy.Romanian authorities said 11 crew members had been rescued and two deceased people had been found. Injured crew members were airlifted by helicopter for medical treatment.The Black Sea has faced heightened security concerns amid the Russia-Ukraine war, with attacks affecting commercial shipping and port infrastructure.The incident came a day after a 52-year-old employee of a pharmaceutical warehouse belonging to Indian owners was killed in a Russian strike in Ukraine's Sumy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy and stepped up efforts in recent months to help resolve the Ukraine conflict by engaging with both Kyiv and Moscow.His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has “good ideas” to find a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.

NEW DELHI: Hours after the Supreme Court clarified that it had not approved any modified version of Form 6, Congress on Monday announced an intensified nationwide campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Party's general secretary KC Venugopal threatened that the agitation over alleged “vote theft” would continue until Kumar is removed and the electoral system is corrected.Announcing the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign, Venugopal said the Congress would take its protest from blocks and villages to the national capital, with marches, chaupals, rallies and a major mobilisation in Delhi planned between October 10 and November 26.“Congress President has given a clear direction today to the PCC Presidents, In-charges, and General Secretaries for an aggressive, nationwide campaign against vote theft - 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao'. This is the slogan we are raising,” he said.The announcement came after a meeting of Congress general secretaries, in-charges, PCC presidents and frontal organisation heads chaired by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and attended by leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.Venugopal said the campaign would not be a short-term protest. “Rahul Gandhi has also given clear directions to our leaders that this agitation is not going to end tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. This will be a continuous, aggressive campaign till Gyanesh Kumar is removed and the system has to be corrected,” he said.The Supreme Court on Monday said it had not approved any modified Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters during the SIR. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified.”Venugopal seized on the development to attack the Election Commission. “You know the Election Commission has become the 'Cheating Commission of India'. After this much - after this much observation from the Supreme Court and the opposition parties, and two Commissioners' remarks also, he is misleading the people,” he said.The first phase of the Congress campaign, from October 10 to 20, will feature block-level bike rallies, cycle rallies and padyatras. “All over India, it will happen. Thousands of workers in each block will participate in this march demanding this thing, and we will burn the effigies of Gyanesh Kumar,” Venugopal said.From October 25 to November 25, Congress workers, whom the party is calling “Vote Rakshaks”, will hold village chaupals and identify voters it alleges have been unfairly deleted from electoral rolls.The campaign will culminate with a mega rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 and six ‘Chalo Delhi’ yatras on November 25 and 26.Venugopal also announced a protest march from Parliament to the Election Commission on Tuesday, saying, “Our aim is to have a peaceful demonstration to show the protest against the Election Commission of India .”“Every person of India wants to remove the Chief Election Commissioner. Only two people want to retain him - Prime Minister and Amit Shah,” he said.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Monday issued a “fact check” amid the controversy over reported changes to Form 6, calling Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s claim that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had “changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally” misleading.In its response, the EC said the order for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar, issued on June 24, 2025, had received the unanimous approval of the Commission and was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court in its judgment dated May 27, 2026.The poll panel also cited its Press Note No. 120 dated September 26, 2026, pointing to point 1(iii), which states: “The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.”The EC's response came after Rahul alleged in a post on X that the CEC had changed Form 6 “illegally and unilaterally”, citing the recent Supreme Court observation.EC officials also clarified that Form 6 itself had not been changed, but that a declaration had been attached to the form under the Bihar SIR order, as quoted by PTI.The clarification came after the Supreme Court said it had not approved any modification to Form 6 used by the EC during the SIR exercise in various states.“Any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When records are produced, we would like to see who has modified it,” a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said.Form 6 is the application used by eligible voters for inclusion in the electoral roll.The declaration was attached to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR, which began with the EC's June 24, 2025 order. The declaration sought additional details, including information about the applicant's parents.According to EC officials, the form itself remained unchanged, while the declaration was a separate document attached to it for the SIR exercise. Outside SIR, the forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply.The declaration was later withdrawn from the EC's online portals.The online version of Form 6 and the declaration also used a single OTP for both, rather than requiring separate OTP verification, which had led to suggestions that the declaration was part of Form 6.The EC also rejected claims that it had withdrawn its September 26 press note and shared the document to show that it remained available.
